titulo: Same Salary, 20 Years Later: One's a Millionaire, One's Broke 💰
descripcion:
Two guys. Same job. Same paycheck. Same tiny apartment. 20 years later, one is a millionaire and the other is broke. Here's why. 👇

Dave spends every paycheck on things: a new phone, a shiny car, a TV the size of a wall. Rich buys boring little slices of companies.
The car loses value the day it's driven home, and the credit card charges about 20% a year. Rich's money quietly makes more money.

That's compound interest. When you own things, the growth starts growing too. Debt is the same snowball, rolling the other way.

The real money game isn't how much you earn. It's what you own.

📊 Facts used:
• US credit card interest averages roughly 20–22% APR (Federal Reserve G.19)
• The top 10% of US households own about 90% of stocks (Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts)
• New cars typically lose 10–20% of their value in the first year
